subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: Should OpenClaw keep automatic bare-text source replies as the default for direct/group/channel sessions, or move channel sessions toward final-only/message-tool-only delivery with an explicit upgrade path?
rationale: The source fix is technically traceable, but the default controls a compatibility-sensitive security boundary: suppressing leaks protects users, while changing automatic replies can silently break existing working channel deployments.

options.title: Adopt final/tool-only policy with upgrade path
options.body: Make non-final channel text private by default where safe, preserve or migrate existing opt-ins, and prove fresh-install plus upgrade behavior across direct, group, cron, and message-tool flows.

options.title: Keep automatic defaults and add narrow guards
options.body: Preserve current compatibility while adding targeted suppression for known commentary/reasoning/tool-envelope patterns, accepting residual leakage risk for unclassified model text.

options.title: Land only opt-in escape hatches
options.body: Review the existing final-tag or verbose-off PR ideas as optional mitigations while leaving the broader default-policy bug open for a later decision.

recommendation.title: Adopt final/tool-only policy with upgrade path
recommendation.body: Make non-final channel text private by default where safe, preserve or migrate existing opt-ins, and prove fresh-install plus upgrade behavior across direct, group, cron, and message-tool flows.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior issue review and recent visible-reply default history point to steipete as the strongest routing candidate for the compatibility/product-policy decision.
